newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST -- Output seen boosting heat stocks in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -- Output seen boosting heat stocks in APIs.

text.p: Thursday evening's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) will likely show a minor build in distillate stocks as a bounce in demand was not enough to absorb feverish production.
"The real key to the build is the high rate of distillate production which has been going on for weeks," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.
An average of trader estimates forecasts distillate stocks -- which consist of heating oil and diesel -- to have grown about 500,000 barrels for the week ended December 27.
The distillate inventory estimates ranged from unchanged to up one million barrels.
Tepid demand is expected to boost gasoline stocks by about one million barrels, with estimates ranging from down 300,000 barrels to up four million barrels.
Crude inventories are expected to decline by about 1.5 million barrels due to tax-related year-end stock reduction. U.S. Gulf refiners are taxed on the amount of crude they hold.
Crude estimates ranged from steady to down four million barrels.
A friendlier arbitrage to the United States from the North Sea could increase crude imports, however, traders said.
No refinery snags kept the utilization rates steady at around 93.3 percent, dealers said. On top of high refinery runs, distillate stock growth will reflect imports from Russia, traders said.

Output was still seen hovering about 3.6 million barrels per day (bpd), only slightly off the 3.8 million bpd record in October. Dealers said the veritable fountain of supply will be offset by shifts to secondary from primary stocks and exports to Europe and South America.
Heat retailers were seen buying simply to keep stocks steady and not because of demand since weather was moderate.
"I've been hearing distributors have been buying heating oil and there is talk of distillate exports to South America," said Jim Ritterbusch, trader with Sweeney Oil in Illinois.
U.S. Gulf refiners have sought to export a surplus of barrels after facing shipment rationing on the Colonial Pipeline which runs from Houston to New York, dealers said.
Colonial extended the rationing through January after getting more shipment requests than its huge distillate line could handle.
"All things being equal - if we don't have huge winter storms - we could eventually end up with a surplus in distillate stocks," said Smith Barney's Saucer.
"Demand has been fine. It's production that has built up supply," he added.
In early August, distillate stocks were 19.8 million barrels below a year ago. Due to stepped up production, the year-over-year shortfall has been reduced to 6.7 million as of December 20.
